Subject: June KPI momentum: dashboard pass & QBR readiness

Team / Sara —

Attached is the June KPI dashboard (v2) and an initial QBR prework checklist. Highlights on the dashboard:
- Latency: 95th p95 is at 220ms (up 12% month-over-month) with a clear spike during the 11–12 PST window on 5/24.
- Cost: token cost per 1k requests rose ~9% after the deployment on 5/18.
- Uptime: 99.93% — still within SLA but trending toward the threshold we discussed last quarter.
- Usage: non-authenticated burst from a partner integration caused an extra 18% of ephemeral traffic on 5/29.

Actions I want us to own before next Tuesday's QBR dry-run:
1) Laura — verify whether the 11–12 PST latency spike correlates with any batch jobs or prefix-cache misses (deliver short RCA).
2) Markus — run a quick cost-profile for the model variants rolled out on 5/18 and recommend one quantization/serve adjustment that recovers at least 4% unit cost.
3) Tessa — consolidate a single page of slides with the dashboard callouts + owner commitments for the exec readout.
4) Sara/Acme — please confirm whether your ops-portal sent repeated health pings on 5/29; if so, can you provide timestamps so we can map traffic to our ingestors?

I've attached the dashboard PDF and a QBR checklist (worksheet) to collect owner confirmations. If you can get first-pass updates in by EOD Monday (6/2) I will collate and circulate an exec-ready packet.

Thanks —
David
David Kim
Head of Platform Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks David — quick read and a few immediate notes.

I pulled traces around the 5/24 11–12 PST window. Preliminary findings:
- Multiple anomalous tail RPCs from a single autoscaler instance (i-az-011) that restarted twice in that window.
- KVCache miss rate is ~3.7x baseline for requests with longer prefixes (~>120 tokens).

I'm attaching the short trace extract (snippet attached) — the stack points to an older runtime kernel that we didn't roll back after the 5/18 push; that kernel has a known mempressure edge case under sustained batch concurrency.

Proposed immediate remediation: pin the 5/18 rollout set to the prior kernel cluster for high-latency traffic until we validate the fix. That should bring p95 back under 200ms. I can own the rollback and a validation test.

On cost — not my lane, but agree we should get a quick delta estimate before we present.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Good call — I ran a cost slice comparing the model mix before/after the 5/18 rollout. Quick summary:
- Variant B (deployed 5/18) increases param-fetch overhead and pushes more requests from optimized kernels to fallback slow-paths; net effect ~+8.7% cost on the affected workload sample.
- If we revert to Variant A for the high-throughput routes and instead enable 4-bit quantization on a canary subset, simulation suggests ~-6% total unit cost with small quality delta.

Action for me: prepare a short cost delta table and two rollout options (rollback vs canary quantization) by Monday morning. Also added a Drive link with the raw compare sheets: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleDriveLink

Two small asks for the QBR packet:
- Tessa: include the rollback cost + canary cost scenarios side-by-side (one slide).
- David/Laura: confirm the timeline for rollback and whether the autoscaler instance replacement needs a separate change window.

-MK
